Comments: On 06/16/2025, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the HIXENBAUGH 1-P060 OG well in West Bethlehem Township, Washington County. The following was observed during inspection:-I observed a slope failure 90x5 ft along access road to well site. The slope failure was found by the Department and not reported. The toe of the slope failure is within access road drainage channel (Photo 1-5). On 04/17/2024 (SAIR 3741762) and 05/10/2024 (SAIR 3760574) stabilization and remediation to access road and channel slope was conducted.-I observed erosion rills and ruts along the access road. I recommend maintenance to access road (Photo 6 and 7).-A well tag was observed on the well head. Some corrosion was observed on well head (Photo 8 and 9).-The well and operator's information were displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h) (Photo 10).-Some corrosion was observed on the production equipment. It appears production equipment was leaking. No elevated conductivity fluid was observed (Photo 11 and 12).-I observed Low Ash Gas Engine Oil/fuel appears to be leaking onto the ground below next to compressor station. I recommend remediation and maintenance to well site (Photo 13-17,20).-Some corrosion was observed on the production tank (Photo 18 and 19).Determination:Violations are being issued for slope failure along access road: 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a)1, and 78.53. Violations are being issued for fuel leaking onto well site. The operator failed to report: 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.54, and SWMA 301

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 9/06/2024 to PENNENERGY RESOURCES LLC in Marion Township, Beaver county. 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNENERGY RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/06/2024
Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8200333
Permit API: 007-20434
Unconventional: Yes
County: Beaver
Municipality: Marion Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/06/2024
Comments: On September 6, 2024, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the 4H well at the B12 well pad. Well appears equipped for production and structurally sound. No leaks, spills, or releases observed at the well head at this time.Gas Production Unit (GPU) is surrounded by secondary containment. Fluid is observed within the secondary containment and two cracks are observed along the concrete curb of secondary containment (Photos 3-6) with wet spots observed outside of the secondary containment in the area of the cracks. Specific conductivity readings were recorded to assist in determining if a possible leak may have occurred. As seen in Photos 7-9, the readings within three separate spots of the containment were 6.82 milliSiemens, 7.36 milliSiemens, and 8.95 milliSiemens. The probe was wiped down to set the reading back to 0.00 before recording the wet spots outside of the containment. The bigger spot observed in Photos 3-4 was recorded at 0.537 milliSiemens and the smaller spot observed in Photos 5-6 was recorded at 1.094 milliSiemens. At this time, it appears that a release of production fluids has occurred from the 4H GPU which was initially contained within secondary containment, but then exited the secondary containment and released to the well pad via the cracks in secondary containment. The release to the well pad appears to be minor at this time. The Department informed Rich Watson of PennEnergy via phone of the release following the inspection.The Department requests information regarding the release including the cause of the release, what was released, the estimated amount of what was released, and details of repairs/remediation efforts.Production tanks are surrounded by secondary containment and appear to be structurally sound this time. No leaks, spills, or releases observed at the production tanks at this time.No erosion and sedimentation (ES) issues observed on the well pad at this time.The original ESCGP-2 (ESX14-007-0005) for this site was issued on 8/1/2014 and was set to expire on 7/31/2019. The ESCGP was renewed as ESCGP-3 on 7/8/2020 with a new expiration date of 7/7/2025. Notice of Termination (NOT) was submitted on 10/19/2022 and was approved to be terminated on 10/25/2022. ESCGP-3 plans are present on site.Violations are being issued for failure to properly manage and control fluids in secondary containment.

Comments: On 6/7/22 at 1305 hrs., I conducted a follow up inspection of Stonehaven Energy Mgt. Co., LLC's Lott 2 well (API 065-26057) in Henderson Twp., Jefferson Co. A Notice of Violation was issued after an inspection conducted by WQSS Shank on 5/19/22 in which a production fluid release was documented (inspection ID 3365343, enforcement 403932). The area around the production fluid tank appears to have fresh pea gravel and spent absorbent pads are still present at the base of the poly tank. The area of the well pad around the well head still remains stained, with signs of stressed and potentially dead vegetation. This area was previously shown to have soil conductivity greater than 20 mS/cm. Additional excavation should be conducted to properly remediate the site. No written response to the NOV issued on 5/24/22 has been received by the Department. No disposal receipts for impacted material has been received by the Department. Violations from inspection ID 3365343 remain outstanding and are being cited again for this inspection. An additional violation of 91.33(b) is being cited for failure to remove residual substances from the ground within 15 days of a pollution incident.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/07/2026 to BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC in Hamilton Township, McKean county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BULL RUN RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/07/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8273599
Permit API: 083-46720
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/07/2026
Comments: I conducted a follow up inspection of this conventional well that had a release occur in November of 2025, when a steel gathering line had ruptured resulting in crude oil contaminating ditches and soil. Initially the remediation of the site was progressing. There had been no signs of product at the under flow dams, there was no viable oil in the ditches. In preperation of obtaining confirmatory soil samples to evaluate if the remediation was sufficient, it was discovered another leak had developed on a different section of the same line. This operator indicated they will replace all of the steel line for this well with plastic/poly line. This release was caught early and as of now, appears to be less than 1 bbl of lost product and has impacted a minimal amount of soil.Bull Run employees had a roll off dumpster en-route to remove the impacted soil. The ruptured line was sucked out with a vac truck and will be removed while running new poly line. Further inspections will be conducted to document ongoing remedation efforts, as well as confirmatory sampling to show that the remediation is sufficient.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/14/2025 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Forks Township, Sullivan county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/14/2025
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8228929
Permit API: 113-20366
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Forks Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/14/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite for a routine inspection. It was about 40 F and overcast.There were 3 wells, 1 produced fluid tank, 3 GPUs, and 1 compressor onsite. There were 2 vent tanks near the wells that were not on secondary containment.Infiltration basins were installed near the northeastern and southeastern pad corners. The basins appeared to be functioning properly. Overall, the site appeared vegetated and stable. There was some erosion observed on the interior of the northeastern basin. There were no other issues noted.It is recommended that the vent tanks be placed on secondary containment. It is also recommended that the interior of the northeastern basin be stabilized.No violations were noted during this inspection, however, violations are outstanding against the 2H well for a release of approximately 1.5 to 2 barrels of produced fluid. The release occurred on 12/25/24 and is documented in inspection 3891330 from 12/26/24. The outstanding violations are for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a).

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 12/08/2022 to DORSO LP in Jefferson Hills Boro, Allegheny county. OGA3220(C) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to notify DEP, the coal operator, lessee and owner prior to plugging a well and submit a plat.
properties.content:

Violation Date: 6/21/2022
Violation Code: OGA3220(C) - PLUGGING REQUIREMENTS - Failure to notify DEP, the coal operator, lessee and owner prior to plugging a well and submit a plat.
Violation ID: 977813
Permit API: 003-21715
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Jefferson Hills Boro
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 12/08/2022
Comments: On 6/20/2022 Howard Drilling LLC began plugging operations on the Dorso LP Matthews #3 Well (003-21715). These operations were completed on 6/21/2022. Notification of Intention by Well Operator to Plug a Well (8000-FM-OOGM0005 Rev. 3/2020) was received by the Department on 6/21/2022. Operator did not provide a date and time of plugging on the submitted NOI. This is a violation of PA Act 13 of 2012 section 3220(c). This section requires the operator to notify the Department of the intention to plug and abandon the well and submit a plat, on a form to be furnished by the Department, showing the location of the well and fixing the date and time at which plugging will commence, which shall be not less than three working days, nor more than 30 days, after the notice is received, to permit a Department representative to be present at the plugging. Operators actions and omissions related to proper submission of the NOI denied the Department the ability to be present at the plugging of the well.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to CNX GAS CO LLC in Morris Township, Greene County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 1/13/2026 to CNX GAS CO LLC in Morris Township, Greene county. 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CNX GAS CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/13/2026
Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 8261805
Permit API: 059-26510
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/13/2026
Comments: On 01/13/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 01/02/2026 at the NV48 Well Site. The Department first received notification of the spill 01/09/2026 from CNX (CTS 39456). I was accompanied by Ralph Barb (PA DEP), Melissa Cherry of Penn E and R, SPSI, and CNX representative Joe Fletcher.Per CNX, spill was said to have been reported to the Departments emergency hotline on 01/02/2026 via the 1 (800) 541-2050 phone number, however the Department did not have a history of a notification. Justin Ruth of CNX submitted a call log of the call, which occurred at 5:48 PM on 01/02/2026.On 01/09/2026, Chad Eisenman of CNX notified the Department of the spill; it was reported that 5 bbls of combined brine and freshwater released onto the pad at the NV48 Well Site on 01/02/2026. The spill was identified at approximately 3:48 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 5:58 PM. Soil and gravel were impacted on the pad, the spill was contained to the pad, and no Waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. CNX is utilizing the alternative spill remediation standards under Act 2.The following was observed during inspection:The spill originated from two produced water tanks (brine) on containment, and a freshwater tank. Produced fluid back-fed into the freshwater tank, and the combined fluids released out of the freshwater tank onto the pad. 5 barrels (bbls) were released (Photo 1).The majority of the impacted material on the pad has been remediated. The impacted area furthest from the tanks yielded conductivity readings ranging from 98.6 - 551 S/cm (Photos 2-6).The surface material was scraped and removed, and trenches/sumps were dug. Conductivity readings within the trenches yielded readings ranging from 1148 S/cm - 3.46 mS/cm (Photos 7-11).Conductivity readings closer to the tanks and the front section of the impacted area ranged from 1469 S/cm - 7.41 mS/cm (Photos 12-18).The area was still in the process of remediation; however it was anticipated to be done the day of the Departments inspection (Photos 19-21).A background conductivity reading was obtained near the edge of the pad. The reading was 655 S/cm (Photos 22, 23).It was noted on site that the roll off dumpster was the fifth one to be used for the waste. I observed incorrect labeling on the roll off (Photo 24).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan were both at the site entrance (Photo 25).Due to the release of production fluid combined with freshwater over a barrel, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

Violation ID: 8258394
Permit API: 111-20223
Unconventional: No
County: Somerset
Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2025
Comments: On December 9, 2025, the Department conducted a Complaint Inspection of Oil and Gas Management Inc's Neilan 1 well site located in Somerset Township, Somerset County.At the time of this inspection, the well site was snow covered, therefore, the vegetative cover of the well site, along with erosion and sedimentation issues throughout the well site and along the access road could not be assessed at the time of this inspection. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a wellhead with a well tag fixed to it that had all required information posted on it. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the wellhead. A small production tank was observed to be connected to the wellhead and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production tank either.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed production equipment connected to a meter box, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near this production equipment or meter box. Inside the Meter Box, the Department observed production paper that was dated 10/27/2023. A pile of pipes was observed on the ground adjacent to the meter box and production equipment, the Department recommends any equipment not in use be removed from the well site. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed two other production tanks on site that both appeared to be connected to the well. The tank on the left did not have any observable holes or corrosive parts, however, the tank on the right had several corroded pipes at the base of the tank and a pipe that was completely broken in half due to corrosion at the top of the tank. No active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near either production tank at this time. A conductivity meter was utilized to screen the area around the right production tank as well as utilized to collect a background soil conductivity reading of 0.234 mS taken upslope and adjacent to the well site. A soil conductivity readings of 1.285 mS was collected below a corroded pipe, and then readings of 0.0089 mS and 0.0694 mS were collected downslope of this area. The reading taken below the corroded pipe is elevated when compared to background, subjugating that a release likely occurred here. The Department is requesting the Operator submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the broken corroded pipe near the top of the production tank and for a release from corroded piping on the production tank.

Permit API: 015-23689
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Wyalusing Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/08/2023
Comments: On 6/8/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a routine site inspection at the Chesapeake Solowiej well site. It was 65 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. I did not screen for conductivity because I did not witness any water puddles or muddy areas on the pad surface during the inspection.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. The site appeared stable and well vegetated, meeting the 70% uniform, perennial, vegetative cover. PCSM is addressed by one sediment pond. The sediment pond is adequately stabilized and was dry at the time of the inspection. I was able to witness an 8 inch riser sticking up about 16 inches from the pond surface. The outlet for the sediment pond overflow drains into a stream alongside the River View roadway. This stream drains to the waters of the Commonwealth. Following an inspection conducted on 10/18/2022, Chesapeake reported that it would make changes to the site to mitigate the issues with the sediment pond. They reported that they were developing a design to accommodate both the drainage and the land owner and hoped to have a finalized plan with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features. There are outstanding violations against the outfall coming off the sediment pond. There were three wells staged for production. All wells were tagged with API/well permit numbers. No bubbling within the cellars was observed. The production tank had secondary containment.The DEP recommends that Chesapeake continues with the process to obtain a revised ESCGP application with the proper drainage and post construction stormwater features and submit to the Department for review.I left the site at 1400 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: XTO ENERGY INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/19/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8265633
Permit API: 019-21494
Unconventional: Yes
County: Butler
Municipality: Summit Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/20/2026
Comments: Melissa Breitenbach (XTO) called the Department on 02/19/2026 to report a release at the well site which occurred at approximately 3:30 PM that day during plugging. I visited the site on 02/20/2026 and met with George Winebark (Operations Supervisor) to gather additional information.Per Mr. Winebark, the release was the result of a valve failure during the circulation stage, which caused an estimated 10 barrels worth of fluid to be expelled. At the time a water truck was on site and managed to collect most of the water as it was being released, which prevented much of it from reaching the ground or spreading off of the pad. The affected area was approximately 15' long and concentrated along a narrow strip where the water flowed. In the attached photographs, the pink flags show the extent of the release per conductivity readings. The highest conductivity readings (> 3.0 mS/cm) were close to the plugging location, and Mr. Winebark attributes these to historical usage (a since-removed production tank) rather than the released fluid, which was largely freshwater. Off pad, readings peaked at 1.8 mS/cm and dropped to 0.035 mS/cm and below within a foot or two. The release does not appear to have traveled more than 5' off pad. There is a stream approximately 500' downslope of the well pad.A section of what appears to be silt fencing seemed to be overwhelmed near the area where the release flowed off pad. The Department recommends repairing or replacing the fencing to prevent future runoff from continuing downslope. Per Ms. Breitenbach, a consultant has been enlisted to assist with Act 2 clean-up, and plugging will continue through the following week. Reclamation and clean-up will begin following the completion of plugging.

Comments: On August 6, 2024, the Department of Oil and Gas inspector, Cody Murray, conducted an onsite inspection of the HERBERT C SMITH 193F (Permit # 021-20853), operated by VESSELS COAL GAS INC.. • There is no visible well posting and no well tag ID on the well anywhere to be found. The hand written ID no longer legible. • The well appears to be not in use. • The well valves are open to the pipeline and the surface is rusted entirely and 4 bolts are missing from the valve flange. • The well head appears intact with no signs of leaking. • OGI used an RKI GX-3R Pro to detect for the presence of gas and no gas was detected. • The 2023 annual production and mechanical assessment reports have not been submitted. • The most recent production report of 2019 indicated the well "Active" - Well Temporarily not producing. • The department requests the operator provide proof of production of the well and when it was last in use. Based on today’s inspections the following violations will be issued: Posting OGA3211(G) - Failure to install permit number and operator information. OGA3211(H) - Failure to install permit number on well. MIA 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. APR 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. 78.121(B) - Failure to electronically submit Annual Production Report to the Department.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/12/2022 to STL RESOURCES LLC in Grugan Twp, Clinton county. CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/12/2022
Violation Code: CSL 401 - PROHIBITION AGAINST OTHER POLLUTIONS - Discharged substance of any kind or character resulting in pollution of Waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 955504
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/12/2022
Comments: On May 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The small berm that was built to collect the seep was was dry and any water that is collected in that area is being vacuumed out. Upon arrival at the well pad, STL Resources was vacuuming water out of the northwest stormwater vault. The conductivity of the water that could not be vacuumed out was 2,500 uS/cm. About 18 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in this vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. STL Resources has back filled and rebuilt the excavated southwest and northwest infiltration berms that were impacted by the spill. DEP screened the water that had pooled up behind the northwest infiltration for conductivity and that resulted in 187 uS/cm. The conductivity of the small amount of water that pooled up behind the southwest infiltration berm was 40 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.1 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 188 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 196.2 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 59.9 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 44.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 133.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. During the inspection, STL Resources consultants were collecting soil samples from the well pad in a grid like pattern to delineate the area of the production fluid spill. Two of the holes that remained open had water pooled in them. Test Pit-209 which was about 7 yards to the north of the northwest stormwater vault had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water in test pit-209 was 2030 uS/cm and soil conductivity was difficult to measure to due the looseness of the soil in the hole. Soil sample 0651-117 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. Test Pit 211 which was about 15 yards to the north of 035-21325, had water pooled in it. The conductivity of the water was 3,800 uS/cm and the soil conductivity was 1,180 uS/cm. Soil Sample 0651-118 was collected from this test pit and will be analyzed for the Bureau of Labs SAC 530. DEP spoke with STL Resources Seth Rodriguez and he said that STL Resources is planning to hydroseed the site's earthen infiltration berms and parts of the site that are lacking vegetation. Infiltration berms 1, 2, 5, 6, and 8 appear to be holding water and not infiltrating within 72 hours. The DEP recommend investigating into the functionality of these berms to avoid over topping or berm erosion. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Fluid removed from the centrifuges is returned to a catch tank and pumped back to the mud tanks for recirculation downhole (photos 3-5). Drill cuttings and excess liquid are solidified using wood crumble material and are stored in steel bins awaiting haulage to the landfill. See photos and comments in the on-site processing findings section of this inspection report below, and refer to the Taft OG-71 Form A application, eFACTS Authorization ID#1525611.Site inspection followed several days of heavy precipitation. A vacuum truck is pumping precipitation water out of secondary containment structures for the frac tank battery at the west side of the pad. The Department observed yellow floc water tanks labeled as cement water near the north side of the rig. The Department recommends that floc water tanks and freshwater tanks near the barite silos be labeled for contents. During this inspection, fluid with elevated conductivity (4.74 mS/cm) is observed in the ditch line between the pad rock and the berm along the north side of the well pad (photo 13). This water was traced and found to be entering Sediment Basin 1 along the rock lined channel sloping down from the pad surface. Additionally, water was observed draining from the sed basin, entering the level spreader, and exiting to a brushy wooded area north of the LOD with a conductivity reading of 2.16 mS/cm. The Department recommends containing and collecting water which exceeds the Department 78a.60b(3) discharge limitation of 1,000 uS/cm or 1 mS/cm. Violations remain outstanding against permit #117-22231 for pollutional water found on site and documented in Inspection Reports #3736567 and #3724668.

Violation ID: 8189736

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 6/04/2024
Comments: On June 4th, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 6/4/24 at 12:04 PM (CTS 381210). Present at today's inspection is William Warfel of Diversified Energy.At the time of this inspection, William stated that at 10:30 AM on 6/4/24 while onsite at the Davenport well, they had noticed some staining on the gravel underneath the production tank valve and a large patch of dead vegetation downslope of the well site. After using measuring devices to gauge the fluid level in the production tank, it was determined that approximately 18-20 barrels had released from the production tank. William stated that prior to the Department arriving onsite, a water truck had already come and emptied the remainder of the production tank. The production tank once empty, was then moved adjacent to where it once sat so that removal of contaminated material could begin. William showed the Department a small area on the valve pipe of the production tank where they believe the leak came from. The Department observed a dried white chalky substance on this area of the valve pipe presumed to be dried brine water. William hypothesizes that the brine water travel down the shale bank adjacent to where the production tank used to sit and pooled in the once grassy lot downslope of the well site.Upon observation of the area downslope of the production tank, the Department noticed an approximately 15ft by 8ft area of dead vegetation and mud with sheeny/iridescent puddles throughout. The Department then took a soil conductivity reading upslope of the production tank in some vegetation adjacent to the well site as a background (0.1337 mS), another in the stained gravel underneath where the production tank valve hole was (1.35 mS), and then on the shale hill leading down to the now dead vegetation adjacent to well site (1.454 mS). Then the Department began taking soil conductivity readings at the bottom of this hill to gauge how wide of an area the spill impacted. A soil conductivity reading was taken in a sheeny/iridescent puddle observed in some mud that was surrounded by dead vegetation (Over range), it was evident that all areas lacking vegetation and that were visibly wet and iridescent were impacted, so the Department went to the edge of this area to determine if any vegetated areas were impacted as well. The dead vegetation looks to be a pathway of where the release may have traveled and it leads right up to a small wooded area. Soil conductivty readings were taken at the edge of the dead vegetation where it meets the wooded area (7.63mS), another taken adjacent to the previous reading in a spot that is also where the dead vegetation meets the woods (5.51 mS), in the wooden area about 1 foot from the dead vegetation (4.90 mS) and even further in the wooded area, about 3 feet in from the dead vegetation (0.1747 mS). A reading was also taken in the grass to the left of the dead vegetation (0.280 mS) to see if that grassy area was impacted as well. These soil conductivity readings subjugate that the impacted area goes beyond where you can visibly see puddles and dead vegetation. While onsite the Department let William know that areas outside of the dead vegetation area are elevated and recommended that when removing contaminated material they give themselves a buffer area larger than 3 feet in each direction. William stated that Spartan Specialty Services would be onsite soon to place impacted soil and gravel into dumpsters and that details will be provided in the Act 2 summary report. William stated that silt fences will also be installed to ensure there are not any erosion and sedimentation issues during the removal process.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for this 18-20 barrel release of brine fluid onto the gravel well site and the adjacent grass lot and wooded area.

Comments: On March 7, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Bozich 2 well in North Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3482092 where it was found that although contaminated soil was removed from the point of impact, contamination from the stockpile was found to be leaching into the soil downslope. Recurring violations were issued as a result. The operator then explained that the tarp which was used to cover it must have been removed by inclement weather, and then proceeded to cover it with reinforced tarp and surround it with straw and silt fence. This was discussed via phone in IR 3483449. As of the date of this Admin inspection, the operator is waiting for the ground to either freeze or thaw enough for machinery to access the well site and remove the excavation stockpile. Kriebel representative Shane Kriebel roughly estimates that 20-25 gallons of fluid escaped from the tank before Kriebel acquired the well site.The following was observed:Heavy tire rutting was observed in the access road leading to the well site (see photo 1). The well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns related to E and S or vegetative coverage (see photos 2 and 3). It was temporarily stabilized and appeared to be establishing vegetation. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the well head (see photo 4), and it was equipped with a well tag (see photo 5). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the formerly impacted areas around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to that of the surrounding soil (see photos 6-8). Additional conductivity readings were taken where contamination from the excavation stockpile was found in IR 3482092 (see photos 9-11). Elevated conductivity was found within 2 feet downslope of the stockpile. A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 230 Microsiemens (see photo 12).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that the point of impact has been remediated and is now recovering. However, contamination from the excavation stockpile may still be impacting the soil downslope, although it does not appear to be spreading. Therefore, closure of violations shall be contingent upon submittal of waste manifest to the Department; removal and proper disposal of the excavation stockpile, and any additional impacted soil discovered underneath or downslope; and a subsequent CEI inspection. Violations remain outstanding.

County: Westmoreland
Municipality: North Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/07/2023
Comments: On March 7, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Bozich 2 well in North Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3482092 where it was found that although contaminated soil was removed from the point of impact, contamination from the stockpile was found to be leaching into the soil downslope. Recurring violations were issued as a result. The operator then explained that the tarp which was used to cover it must have been removed by inclement weather, and then proceeded to cover it with reinforced tarp and surround it with straw and silt fence. This was discussed via phone in IR 3483449. As of the date of this Admin inspection, the operator is waiting for the ground to either freeze or thaw enough for machinery to access the well site and remove the excavation stockpile. Kriebel representative Shane Kriebel roughly estimates that 20-25 gallons of fluid escaped from the tank before Kriebel acquired the well site.The following was observed:Heavy tire rutting was observed in the access road leading to the well site (see photo 1). The well site appeared to be stable at the time of inspection, with no concerns related to E and S or vegetative coverage (see photos 2 and 3). It was temporarily stabilized and appeared to be establishing vegetation. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the well head (see photo 4), and it was equipped with a well tag (see photo 5). Soil conductivity readings were taken in the formerly impacted areas around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to that of the surrounding soil (see photos 6-8). Additional conductivity readings were taken where contamination from the excavation stockpile was found in IR 3482092 (see photos 9-11). Elevated conductivity was found within 2 feet downslope of the stockpile. A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 230 Microsiemens (see photo 12).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that the point of impact has been remediated and is now recovering. However, contamination from the excavation stockpile may still be impacting the soil downslope, although it does not appear to be spreading. Therefore, closure of violations shall be contingent upon submittal of waste manifest to the Department; removal and proper disposal of the excavation stockpile, and any additional impacted soil discovered underneath or downslope; and a subsequent CEI inspection. Inspection Date: 3/03/2023
Comments: Site inspection by EPS Justin Abbott. Inspection conducted in response to spill notification submitted by EQT for the Salt Run HC EXT Pad A location. Inspection accompanied by EQT Company Man Matt Casler and EQT Senior EHS Coordinator Zac Subra. Weather conditions at time of inspection are overcast and 38 degrees F. Well stimulation activity is ceased at this time while the spill response is ongoing.According to the Emergency Response Notification Report submitted by EHS supervisor Rick Hall, 'approximately one barrel of production fluid was released to the pad surface off containment and approximately 50 barrels of production fluid were released on containment at the Salt Run Pad A Extension. EQT was in the middle of a frac on the pad when a pipe came apart and spilled the production fluid onto containment and soil. Tobias Machining and Welding was contracted to perform remediation worm on the impacted soils. No waterways or stormwater structures were impacted.'During site inspection and discussions with Mr. Subra and Mr. Casler, the following details were reported. Universal Pressure Pumping was conducting a zipper frac of four wells at the time of the incident. At around 2:19 AM, while fracturing stage 11 of the 11H well (API #081-21907) the high pressure iron pipe connecting the frac missile to the well head failed resulting in a high pressure release of production fluid and frac sand. The fluid pressure at the time of the incident was 9,450 PSI and the pumping volume was 90 barrels per minute of the slurry mixture. The fluid release was brought under control in 20 seconds. Due to the pressure of the release, the slurry mixture of sand and fluid sprayed vertically into the air with a majority landing in secondary containment while an unknown volume landed on the pad rock surface along the south side of the pad. The affected area outside containment is an L-shaped section along the south access way approximately 200' by 15' with another area of 50 by' 50' affected adjacent to the Modular Aboveground Storage Structure (Photos 3,6 and 7). At time of inspection, Matt Tusing with Penn E and R is delineating the edges of the affected pad surface. A skidsteer is scraping affected pad material and placing it into a lined steel rolloff container. According to Mr. Subra, three rolloffs are reserved for pad rock material, each capable of holding 18 tons of material. Scraped pad rock will be staged in the lined containers at the Salt Run Pad B location pending analysis. Two vac trucks are on site to vacuum production fluid from the containment surface. A pressure washing crew is en route to clean fluid and sand from the secondary containment structure. Due to the volume of fluid which was released from the failed high pressure fitting and the unknown volume of fluid released to the pad surface, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation. Mr. Subra indicated that Act 2 remediation will be undertaken by EQT. Violations noted.

Violation ID: 8210443

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/06/2024
Comments: On 12/06/2024, an incident inspection was conducted at the Henderson Well Site following receipt of an incident report, submitted on 12/04/2024, following a spill (CTS 385605). I was accompanied by DJ Hardy (EQT).On 12/04/2024, it was reported that approximately 20 gallons of brine water was spilled on the well pad following a dump line washout. EQT intends to remediate through Act 2 guidelines. EQT shared that it did not appear that there were any impacts off of the pad and the sumps did not appear impacted. The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance and the emergency response plan was in the mailbox (Photo 1).Material had been excavated from around the dump line behind the 15H Gas Production Unit (GPU) (Photos 2, 3). The elbow joint on the dump line was the origin of the spill (Photos 4, 5).Conductivity readings around the origin were 2.25, 2.37, and 6.26 mS/cm (Photos 6-8).The main dump line was also exposed with material excavated (Photo 9).Readings along the main dump line were 2.28, 4.04, 4.57, 5.56, and 7.28 mS/cm (Photos 10-14).A test pit was excavated to determine the extent of impacted material. The pit was filled and no elevated conductivity was noted in the area (Photo 15).No stressed vegetation noted and no elevated conductivity within vegetation (Photo 16). Bank was cut for access.A vac truck removed material from the excavated pits and was in a container on site (Photo 17).Additional material labeled was on site (Photos 18, 19).Due to the release of production fluid to to pad, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/03/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8215839
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/03/2025
Comments: On 02/03/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 0915 hours, weather was 33F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.There are 2 recently drilled wells located onsite which are currently undergoing flow back as a result of the completion of hydraulic fracturing activities; well permits are posted with the Act 9 sign at the site entrance (photos #1 and 2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are not yet in use but are held in a secondary containment structure. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the tanks are not yet labeled, and I discussed the need to label them with personnel onsite; they informed me that they would be labeled after they dried off. Two modular aboveground storage structures (MASS's) are located onsite to hold brine during flow back, and a lined residual waste container is located next to them and held on containment (photo #5). Multiple upright brine and temporary storage tanks for holding produced fluids during flow back are also noted onsite; all tanks are held in secondary containment which appears to be functioning as intended (photos #6 and 7).Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed due to snow coverage. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review at the site entrance and is up to date (photo #8). One infiltration basin serve as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) controls (photo #9). No standing water was observed in the PCSM control it appears to be functioning as intended.The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962.No violations noted. I departed the site at 1015 hours.
